small_guidance:
- The GEMM is M=128, N=K=16384 — M is tiny so BLOCK_M=32 or 64 is right, but add larger BLOCK_N (256) with BLOCK_K=64 and num_stages=4 to better hide the long K-loop latency. Add a GROUP_M block-swizzle (e.g. GROUP_M=8) on the (pid_m, pid_n) grid for L2 reuse across N tiles.
- Softmax: N=16384 fits in registers if you use BLOCK_SIZE=16384 with num_warps=16 (or 32) — drop the three-pass loop in favor of a single-pass online softmax (running max + running sum) over BLOCK_SIZE chunks, eliminating two full re-reads of the row from HBM.
- Fuse the softmax directly on the GEMM output by writing a persistent epilogue kernel, or at minimum skip the dropout no-op branch at eval (already the case) and ensure `weight_t` and `bias` are moved to CUDA in `__init__` so `forward` doesn't redo `.contiguous().cuda()` on every call.
large_guidance:
- Replace the separate GEMM + softmax kernels with a fused "linear + softmax" persistent kernel: one program per row (or small row-block), keep the M-row tile of x resident, stream over N in BLOCK_N chunks computing partial dots against weight columns, and run an online softmax (max/sum running stats) over the produced N values in registers — then a second pass over N recomputes the dot and writes `exp(z - max)/sum`. This avoids materializing the full (128, 16384) logits to HBM twice.
- Alternatively, treat the problem as a tall-skinny GEMM (M=128) with a row-resident strategy: load the entire x row tile (BLOCK_M, K) once into SRAM/registers and stream weight columns; with M=128 and K=16384 this fits comfortably and removes redundant x-loads across N tiles.
- Move all .cuda()/contiguous() and weight transpose work into __init__ once; forward should only launch kernels.
